scope: Exploratory post-test diagnosis after all six frozen WaterHub periods completed. Not fresh validation, not a tuned replacement, and no additional generalization evidence. Only saved scores, frozen choices, metrics and trusted fitted bundles were read; no fitting/threshold search/prediction changes.
limitations: Binary minute labels are an OR across six annotation streams; these records do not establish physical fault types.
Saved score separation and calibrated conservatism describe associations, not a causal proof that another threshold/method would meet false-alarm limits.
GECCO versus WaterHub differences conflate domain, sampling/label aggregation and event definitions. No universal physical event-duration comparison is claimed.

findings.claim: Weak event detection is not explained by unavailable observations or continuing-alarm accounting.
findings.interpretation: The IF ranking plus its past-calibrated operating point rarely enters alarm during labeled events. This is not evidence that lowering its threshold would satisfy false-alarm constraints.

findings.claim: Alarms are extremely sparse relative to the long labeled-positive intervals, explaining the low point F1.
findings.interpretation: An occasional onset hit can count an event while covering very little of its duration; event recall and point F1 therefore tell materially different stories.

findings.claim: The source has longer positive intervals and a different annotation/data regime than GECCO.
findings.interpretation: WaterHub pressure and OR-of-six-stream minute labels differ from GECCO multichannel water-quality labels. This supports a domain/annotation mismatch hypothesis, not a verified taxonomy of changed physical fault types.

findings.claim: The saved calibration outcomes already show low sensitivity at the false-alarm-constrained operating points.
findings.interpretation: Strict no-added-FP and event-identity safeguards preserve a weak reference, and compounded local/movement/shape gates leave very sparse rescue evidence. No alternative threshold was evaluated on the test data.

findings.claim: Suppression only reduced false alarms in February for concrete gate-availability reasons.
findings.interpretation: Unknown gate evidence deliberately retains IF, and the latch deliberately prevents splitting an already-retained alarm. Those safeguards help explain noninferiority without recurrent false-alarm gains.

findings.claim: The nine extra detected events came from two distinct selected rescue paths.
findings.interpretation: March gains must not be attributed to the local-change or jump branch: the frozen generic selector chose the raw shape classifier. Its branch does not require local movement evidence.

findings.claim: Rescue gains did not persist across all later periods.

evidence.2018-12_and_2019-01: No rescue trial satisfied the saved joint calibration constraints.

findings.interpretation: The calibration-to-test shift in score support is visible in April; sparse isolated evidence is additionally rejected by the unchanged persistence rule. This describes the observed failure, not a proposed retuning.

findings.claim: The frozen validation acceptance remains false despite aggregate improvement and no lost reference events.
findings.interpretation: The objective of stable improvement has not been achieved. Audit success verifies calculations/replay, not detection quality or deployment readiness.

next_direction_not_implemented: A future method should model sustained within-event evidence for longer pressure regimes while keeping an independent IF reference and original-axis availability/event-ID audits. Any change needs newly declared development and later genuinely unused evaluation; this test is now disclosed and cannot be reused as fresh evidence.
